The two lines overlap at sessions 2, 6, 7 and 8, so the markers at session 8 cannot be separated reliably. No error bars, gridlines, annotations or patient identifiers are visible.

visual.general_description: Three clinical photographs of legs and feet with adhesive electrodes and cables above a labelled front-and-back dermatome diagram with hand-drawn colored electrode position marks on one leg.
visual.detailed_description: Composite of three color photographs above one color anatomical diagram, with no printed panel letters. Photograph 1 (left): a seated person with bare lower legs hanging over an examination table; several small white adhesive electrode pads with thin cable leads are on the thigh/knee region and near the ankle and top of the foot, with yellow, red, blue and orange connector clips and loose wires on the floor; the face is not shown. Photograph 2 (middle): close-up of the sole of a bare foot with a white pad and yellow clip near the ankle and a white pad with a green clip near the heel, bundled cables running down, and a medical device with a display screen and colored cable ports in the background; the screen text is not legible. Photograph 3 (right): rear view of a standing person from the lower thigh to the feet, with one large pad with a black connector behind the knee, a smaller pad with a black connector on the calf, and pads with red, blue and yellow connectors at the ankles; dark shorts, a dark shoe and a white cloth on the floor are visible; the face is not shown. The diagram below is titled "DERMATOMES" and shows a front view and a back view of a human body colored by dermatome, labelled C2 to C8, T1 to T12, L1 to L5, S1 to S5 and Co1, with "NV Trigeminal" on the head and the italic text "Each area of skin is labeled with the nerve that innervates it." Hand-drawn blue dots joined by thin lines run down the leg on the right side of the front view, ending at a dot with the handwritten blue label "plantar foot". Hand-drawn red dots joined by thin lines run down the leg on the right side of the back view to the foot. The drawn marks lie over the L5, S1 and nearby regions of the leg.
